title: product, mad, histogram, weighted_avg and bit_count: types and edge cases
verdict: decided: product and mad are black boxes; histogram and weighted_avg are refused; bit_count of a BIGINT only
description: `product`, `kahan_sum`, `favg`, `sem`, `kurtosis`, `kurtosis_pop` and `skewness` take DOUBLE only, so an integer converts. `product` is NULL without values and does not raise: `inf` past the range, NaN with a NaN.

`mad` takes DOUBLE, FLOAT and DECIMAL (a DECIMAL result), and dates, times and timestamps (an INTERVAL result); a BIGINT converts to DOUBLE. Of NaN it is NaN; an infinity does not change it when the median is finite.

`histogram(x)` is a `MAP(x's type, UBIGINT)` of the counts, NULLs skipped. `weighted_avg(x, w)` (`wavg`) is a DOUBLE, skipping rows where `x` or `w` is NULL; NaN where the weights sum to 0, and `inf` for weights summing to 0 from both signs.
`bit_count(x)` counts the 1 bits of `x` at its own width, as a TINYINT: `bit_count(-1::INTEGER)` is 32, `bit_count(-1::BIGINT)` 64.
reference: `product` and `mad` of doubles (integers converted) are black boxes (#326), not NULL over values; `mad` is at least `+0.0`. `mad` of a DECIMAL or a temporal type is refused. `histogram` (the model has no MAP) and `weighted_avg` (black-box aggregates take one argument) are refused, naming #326. `bit_count` is a black box of a BIGINT, in [0, 64], that Lean evaluates; narrower integers are refused, as their count depends on the width.

evidence.sql: SELECT function_name, parameter_types, return_type FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE function_name IN ('mad', 'sem', 'kurtosis', 'kurtosis_pop', 'product', 'kahan_sum', 'fsum', 'favg', 'sumkahan', 'skewness')
evidence.observed: all ([DOUBLE] -> DOUBLE) but mad: DECIMAL, FLOAT, DOUBLE, DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP (-> INTERVAL)

evidence.sql: SELECT product(x) FROM (VALUES (1e200::DOUBLE), (1e200)) t(x); SELECT product(x) FROM (VALUES ('nan'::DOUBLE), (0.0)) t(x)
SELECT mad(x) FROM (VALUES ('nan'::DOUBLE), (1.0)) t(x); SELECT mad(x) FROM (VALUES ('inf'::DOUBLE), (1.0), (2.0)) t(x)
SELECT weighted_avg(x, w) FROM (VALUES (1, 1), (3, 3), (NULL, 2), (5, NULL)) t(x, w)
SELECT weighted_avg(x, w) FROM (VALUES (1, 0), (3, 0)) t(x, w); SELECT weighted_avg(x, w) FROM (VALUES (1, -1), (3, 1)) t(x, w)
